newsitem.title: USA: AWAY ON BUSINESS: Travel tips.
newsitem.headline: AWAY ON BUSINESS: Travel tips.

text.p: Assorted news of interest to business travelers:
Puddle Jumping Jets
Commuter airline passengers will be seeing more and more jets replacing turboprops on those busy short-haul flights, in an industry response to both the need for speed and perceived safety concerns.
That information comes from a report in the March issue of Frequent Flyer magazine that says a number of feeder carriers have ordered jets, most commonly 50-passenger Canadair CRJs or Embraer 145s.

Among the regional carriers with jets on order or already in their fleets are Air Wisconsin-United Express, Atlantic Southeast-Delta Connection, Continental Express, Mesaba-Northwest Airlink, Comair-Delta Connection, SkyWest Delta Connection, Horizon Air, Mesa Airlines and Mesa Air-America West Express, the report said.
Information on the magazine con be obtained at 1-800-323-3537
Working Rooms
The lodging industry's efforts to provide travelers with convenient in-room working environments continues to expand.
Budgetel Inns Inc., which has 135 company-owned or franchised properties, says it is turning 10 percent of its rooms at each location into business-class facilities.

The amenities will include telephone lines that are modem-friendly, desk-top lamps with better lighting and convenient power outlets to save the guest from crawling around looking for a place to plug in a laptop.
Expensive Cities

Hong Kong, at $474 a day, is the most expensive city in the world in which to do business business in terms of per-day costs for hotels and meals, according to a report from Runzheimer International, a Wisconsin-based management consulting firm.

The others in the top five are Tokyo ($440), Moscow ($392), Buenos Aires ($383) and Paris ($377). The figures are based on the average business traveler's cost for breakfast, lunch and dinner in business-class restaurants and single-rate lodging in a business class hotel or motel.
The firm said it was the "first time in memory" that Hong Kong had bested Toyko for most expensive honours in its periodic surveys.
Airline Ratings
A new survey of airlines offering business class service has found Continental Airlines tops among domestic carriers. Among foreign airlines Virgin Atlantic took top honours.

The survey, appearing Smart Money Magazine, was based on dozens of factors such as legroom, seat size and configuration as well as ease of upgrade, on-time performance, frequent flier programmes and fleet age.
Among domestic carriers, after Continental, the others in order were United, American, Northwest, USAirways, TWA, and Delta.
The rankings for carriers based outside the United States, after Virgin Atlantic, were Air Canada, British, Qantas, Swissair, Singapore, Lufthansa, KLM, SAS, Air France, ANA and Japan Airlines.
The complete survey can be found in the April issue of the magazine, avaliable at newsstands, or by calling 1-800-444-4204.
Clean Hands
An Ohio company that makes an "instant hand sanitizer" is touting it as the answer for travelers on the run who might not have time to find a sink and a bar of soap.
The gel-like lotion, called Purell, evaporates after being rubbed on the hands, leaving them dry and 99 percent germ free, the company says.

It was tested recently at free-standing kiosks at the Akron-Canton Regional Airport where travelers walking through terminals were invited to "wash" and run -- and buy the product at the gift shop if they liked it.
A spokeswoman for the company said travelers may be seeing other tests in other locations. The product is available at drug stores, grocery stores and other retailers.

Business travelers: Question, complaint or pet peeve? Send them to Away on Business, c/o Reuters, Room 1170, 311 S. Wacker Dr., Chicago 60606. Or via e-mail to Mike.Conlon(at)Reuters.com using. We cannot promise personal replies but will try to address letters as space permits.
